newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA'S LEISURENET BUYS PRO SHOP FOR 70 MLN RAND.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA'S LEISURENET BUYS PRO SHOP FOR 70 MLN RAND.

text.p: South African health and food franchise group LeisureNet said on Thursday it has bought golfing retail outlet Pro Shop for 70 million rand.

Financial director Mico Smuts said the deal was the firm's biggest acquisition to date. The buy, which will be effective from December 1, will be financed through the issue of 9.3 million shares at 380 cents each.

"If the profit warranty - which states that profit before tax should not be less than 9.1 million rand for the period ending June 30, 1997 - is met, LeisureNet has undertaken to issue, subject to JSE approval, a further 8.8 million shares at 400 cents a share," Smuts said.
"We have adhered to our growth strategy by once again acquiring a financially strong business...that, as with our other operations, are cash generators."
The Pro Shop was formed in 1976 and has cornered almost 50 percent of the golf market in South Africa. It has four retail outlets and three franchise stores.

Smuts said that the acquisition would have no material effect on LeisureNet's estimated earnings for the year to December 31, 1996 but would make a "significant contribution to bottom-line earnings in the new financial year."
